task.title: Fix payment client timeouts
task.description: Payment requests intermittently time out under load. Propose a safe fix consistent with the existing retry constraints.

proposal.summary: Keep retry and timeout settings unchanged; address load-related timeouts through connection pooling, HTTP keep-alive reuse, and phase-specific timeout observability.
plan_steps: Instrument the payment client to record timeout phase (pool wait, connect, read), pool usage, and connection reuse.
Size the per-host connection pool from recorded pool-wait and concurrency evidence and enable or retain HTTP keep-alive reuse.
Reassess timeout or retry changes only after phase metrics identify the timeout source and any documented ceiling is confirmed.

claims.statement: The proposed change leaves the existing payment-client maximum retry attempts, retryable conditions, and backoff settings at their values in the stored project records; no value is increased or added.
The proposed change introduces no new retry path: a timed-out payment request is submitted no more times than the existing retry policy already permits.
The proposed change leaves the existing per-request payment timeout value unchanged and changes only connection-pool sizing, HTTP keep-alive reuse, and timeout-phase observability.

assumptions: Pool-wait or connection-reuse contention under load is a contributing cause; this is an expectation, not confirmed by records provided in the task description.
The payment service and network can accept additional persistent connections within their existing limits.
Phase-specific timeout metrics can identify whether timeouts occur during pool wait, connection establishment, or reading the response before any timeout value is changed.
uncertainties: No stored records were provided in the task description, so the existing retry cap, retryable conditions, backoff policy, and timeout ceiling cannot be confirmed here.

The root cause is not provided: records do not establish in the task description whether timeouts are caused by pool exhaustion, server latency, network latency, or another factor, so the appropriate pool size is not settled.
Idempotency-key support for payment submissions and downstream limits on persistent connections are not provided in the task description.

evidence.content: Fact: the payment-client test constraint_cap_is_three_attempts fails for any RetryPolicy with max_attempts above 3 or with jitter_ms equal to 0.
Fact: send_with_retries in payment-client retries only SendError::Timeout, up to RetryPolicy.max_attempts; upstream errors are returned at once without a retry.
Fact: in the 2026-08 outage, retry bursts from payment clients amplified an upstream slowdown into a full outage.
Decision (2026-09 payments review): fix payment timeouts by setting the payment-client RetryPolicy to max_attempts = 3 with jitter_ms of at least 50; raising the attempt cap above 3 is not allowed.
Fact: payment client timeouts correlate with retry bursts above 5 attempts.
Fact: the payment-client default RetryPolicy is max_attempts = 1 with jitter_ms = 0, so a single transient upstream timeout surfaces to users as a payment timeout.

items.description: Leaving the retry policy unchanged conflicts with the 2026-09 payments decision requiring max_attempts = 3 and jitter_ms of at least 50, because the current default is max_attempts = 1 with jitter_ms = 0.
Retaining jitter_ms = 0 leaves a RetryPolicy that fails the existing constraint_cap_is_three_attempts test, which fails when jitter_ms equals 0.

The proposal provides no test or classification rule showing that new pool-wait timeouts will not be mapped to SendError::Timeout and enter the existing retry loop, even though send_with_retries retries that error and retry bursts previously amplified an upstream slowdown into an outage.

The pooling and keep-alive plan does not establish pool exhaustion as the timeout cause, while the records instead show that the default single-attempt policy causes a single transient timeout to surface to users as a payment timeout.

Increasing per-host pool size and persistent connection reuse without confirmed downstream connection limits or a load test creates a regression risk under upstream slowdown, a failure mode already documented when client-side bursts amplified the 2026-08 outage.

assessments.note: No Valid record directly states the proposal leaves retry settings unchanged. Valid records show current max_attempts=1 and jitter_ms=0, conflicting with the decision requiring max_attempts=3 and jitter_ms>=50 and with the test failing at jitter_ms=0.

No Valid record states the proposal creates no new retry path or excludes pool-wait timeouts from SendError::Timeout. Valid records show that error is retried and that retry bursts amplified an outage.

No Valid record directly states the timeout value remains unchanged or that only pooling, keep-alive, and observability change. Valid records instead identify the single-attempt policy as surfacing transient timeouts and document burst-related outage risk.

proposal.summary: Revise the fix to follow the 2026-09 payments decision: set RetryPolicy to max_attempts = 3 and jitter_ms = 50, retain the existing Timeout-only retry path, and drop the unsupported pooling and keep-alive changes.
plan_steps: Change the payment-client default RetryPolicy from max_attempts = 1 and jitter_ms = 0 to max_attempts = 3 and jitter_ms = 50; do not raise max_attempts above 3.

Remove the connection-pool sizing and HTTP keep-alive changes from this proposal, so this revision introduces no new pool-wait timeout type or classification into SendError::Timeout and no increase in persistent connections.
Run constraint_cap_is_three_attempts with max_attempts = 3 and jitter_ms = 50.

Add or verify attempt-count tests: SendError::Timeout is retried only up to 3 total attempts, an upstream error is returned after one attempt without retry, and no error other than SendError::Timeout enters the retry loop.

Monitor per-request attempt counts, aggregate retry volume, and payment timeout rates after rollout, given the documented 2026-08 retry-burst outage; investigate if aggregate retries amplify an upstream slowdown despite the cap of 3 and jitter.

claims.statement: The revised RetryPolicy sets max_attempts = 3 and jitter_ms = 50, replacing the stored default of max_attempts = 1 and jitter_ms = 0 and satisfying the 2026-09 decision requiring max_attempts = 3 with jitter_ms of at least 50 without raising the cap above 3.
Retries remain in the existing send_with_retries path, which retries only SendError::Timeout up to RetryPolicy.max_attempts and returns upstream errors at once without retry.
A RetryPolicy with max_attempts = 3 and jitter_ms = 50 avoids the constraint_cap_is_three_attempts failure conditions of max_attempts above 3 or jitter_ms equal to 0.

assumptions: Setting max_attempts = 3 and jitter_ms = 50 is expected to reduce user-visible transient payment timeouts, as intended by the 2026-09 decision.
Jitter of 50 ms is expected to help spread retries, although the records do not prove a specific jitter value above the required minimum is optimal.
uncertainties: The records do not provide a load-test result for max_attempts = 3 with jitter_ms = 50 under upstream slowdown, so aggregate retry-burst risk still requires monitoring given the 2026-08 outage.
The records specify jitter_ms of at least 50 but do not identify a preferred value above 50.

evidence.content: Constraint: outbound retries must be capped at 3 attempts with jitter; unbounded retries caused the 2026-08 outage.
